key_insight: HERMES++ presents a unified driving world model that simultaneously performs 3D scene understanding and future scene generation, bridging semantic reasoning and geometric prediction in a single framework.
problem_solved: Current driving world models either generate future scenes or focus on 3D understanding, and LLMs provide strong semantic reasoning but lack geometric future prediction—HERMES++ addresses this fragmentation by combining both capabilities in one model.
method: Learn a shared 3D latent world representation that encodes geometry, semantics, and dynamics for driving environments.
Train the model in a multi-task, multimodal setup (sensor inputs → unified latent) to support both accurate scene understanding and realistic future scene generation.
Integrate semantic reasoning modules with physical prediction components so the model can produce temporally consistent, semantically rich 3D simulations useful for planning and evaluation.
impact: By unifying understanding and generation, HERMES++ enables richer, more interpretable simulation for autonomous driving — improving downstream tasks like planning, validation, and synthetic data creation while narrowing the gap between language-level reasoning and physical scene evolution.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: sensors → shared 3D latent world model → branches for understanding (perception/labels) and generation (future scenes).
Before vs after comparison: separate perception/generation pipelines contrasted with the unified HERMES++ pipeline.
Temporal evolution strip: sequence of 3D scene snapshots showing predicted geometric change over time.
Icon set: sensor inputs (LiDAR/camera), semantic tags, physics/dynamics arrows, and an LLM-style reasoning bubble to show integration.
paper_title: HERMES++: Toward a Unified Driving World Model for 3D Scene Understanding and Generation
paper_authors: Xin Zhou, Dingkang Liang, Xiwu Chen, Feiyang Tan, Dingyuan Zhang
